user.text: Keep related products out of the default product-page prefetch, but have them ready immediately when navigating from the featured-product link.

history.assistant:
A default link to `/product` no longer prefetches related products, but the featured-product link does, so they're there as soon as the page opens. The build passes. I didn't test the prefetch behavior itself in a browser.

This uses Next.js 16.4's partial prefetching, following the docs bundled in `node_modules/next`:

1. **`next.config.ts`**: added `partialPrefetching: true`. With it on, a default `<Link>` prefetches only the route's shared "App Shell" (the part of the page that's the same for every link).
2. **`app/product/page.tsx`**: moved the related products into a `RelatedProducts` component inside `<Suspense>`. It calls `await prefetch()` from `next/cache` before `getRelatedProducts()`. That keeps the list out of the default prefetch, which gets only the "Loading related products..." fallback. A link with `prefetch={true}`, or the navigation itself, still loads the list. `getRelatedProducts()` still caches for hours as before.
3. **`app/page.tsx`**: the featured link is now `<Link href="/product" prefetch={true}>`, so it fetches the related products before the click.

Checks:
- `npx next build` finished with exit code 0. TypeScript passed and `/product` still prerenders statically (revalidate 1h, expire 1d).
- With `next start`, the first load of `/product` still includes the related products in the HTML (`prefetch()` doesn't affect a first page load).

To confirm the navigation behavior itself, you'd need an `instant()` test with `@next/playwright`, which the docs describe. It would click the featured link and check that the related products show up with no fallback.

Setting `partialPrefetching: true` changes default prefetching for every route. That's harmless here, since this is the only link and nothing used `prefetch={true}` before. If you'd rather limit it to one route, you can instead add the `prefetch = 'partial'` setting to that route's segment config.

The build also rewrote `tsconfig.json` and created `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts`. I undid all three. Your existing `package.json` change and the untracked `package-lock.json` are untouched.

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.

## Use the adoption skill (recommended)

The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.

Install the skill:

```bash filename="Terminal"
npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
```

Then give the agent this prompt:

```prompt
Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
```

## Or adopt by hand

To adopt an existing app by hand:

1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.

Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay wi

19:
20:Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.
21:
22:With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), a [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) prefetches one reusable [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route by default. The App Shell includes the route's static output. For routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), it also includes session-specific UI. Links to the same route reuse that App Shell.
23:
24:The shared App Shell does not include URL data that varies by destination, such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional). Set `prefetch={true}` on a link to resolve cached content that depends on its [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) before navigation instead of streaming that content after navigation.
25:
26:This guide assumes [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled:
27:
28:```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5}
29:import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
30:
31:const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
32:  cacheComponents: true,
33:  partialPrefetching: true,
34:}
35:
36:export default nextConfig
37:```
38:
39:It also assumes your route is already structured for instant navigation. If it isn't, start with the [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) to validate its caching structure first.
40:
41:## Resolve URL data at prefetch time
42:
43:Set `<Link prefetch={true}>` to resolve URL data for that link before navigation. The destination must use [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), enabled globally with `partialPrefetching` or per segment with [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch#partial).
44:
45:A user on `/` sees links to `/search?q=react` and `/search?q=next`, each opting in with `prefetch={true}`:
46:
47:```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
48:import Link from 'next/link'
49:
50:export default function Home() {
51:  return (
52:    <nav>
53:      <Link href="/search?q=react" prefetch={true}>
54:        React
55:      </Link>
56:      <Link href="/search?q=next" prefetch={true}>
57:        Next.js
58:      </Link>
59:    </na
